decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed display of animated advertisements, by reason of insufficient site-specific evidence and the introduction of moving imagery in a visually sensitive roadside location, would be likely to result in distraction to highway users, to the detriment of highway and pedestrian safety. The application fails to demonstrate that the proposal would not cause harm having regard to the proximity of a pedestrian crossing and the identified limitations of the supporting evidence, including the absence of detailed information on the specific site context and the reliance on strategic, non site-specific research. Furthermore, the proposed reliance on a VAMM threshold would not provide a precise or enforceable mechanism to control the level of motion. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies D4 (Advertisements) and T1 (Prioritising walking, cycling and public transport) of the Camden Local Plan 2017.

Reason : 2 - The proposed display of animated advertisements, would draw the eye excessively, add visual clutter and by reason of the visual dominance would harm the character and appearance of the streetscene, the adjacent positive contributors and the wider conservation area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies D1 (Design), D2 (Heritage) and D4 (Advertisements) of the Camden Local Plan 2017.
